An animation is one type: a value for a time, and when it next changes (rich-animation-42lg.8yz)

`Animation<T>` (src/core/animation.ts) is `at(t)` and `nextChange(t)`, with
`constant`, `continuous`, `map` and `sequence`. The existing motion is now
instances of it rather than a second notion of "when it next changes":

- `Beat.end` is `Beat.nextChange`, so a beat is an `Animation<number>`.
- `FrameSequence.text(t)` is `at(t)`, plus `nextChange(t)`; its cells are
  stamped with that one answer.
- `Spinner` gains `nextChange(t)`: the sooner of its two sequences, since the
  output picks which one draws.
- `Effect` is `(drawn) => Animation<EffectFrame>`. `withNextChange` and
  `nextChangeOf` are gone; `onBeat`, `confined`, `steppedInk` and
  `stillOnSlots` are built on the animation (steppedInk is the beat mapped to
  inks).

`sequence` carries the next part's change back onto the shared timeline
through `walkUp`, the float walk `beat` already used, now shared from
easing.ts. docs/animation.md is the toolbox's page; effects, frames and easing
point at it.

Spring, bounce and overshoot curves join the easing vocabulary (rich-animation-42lg.4zu)

`spring({ stiffness, damping, mass })` is a damped harmonic oscillator as an
`Ease`, and since how long a spring rings is a fact about its physics, it
comes with the `seconds` it settles in (to within `SPRING_REST`), so
`{ ...spring(…), swing }` is an effect's `Curve`. Beside it, Penner's
`bounce`, `back-in`, `back-out` and `elastic` at his constants. All five are
named in `EASES` and parse by name. One `settled` wrapper holds every physics
ease to [0, 1] and to exactly 1 at its end, so a count eased by one lands on
its target.

Pinned against the integrated equation of motion in every damping regime
and against Penner's values at the quarter points; sampled through
`Phase.once` at one frame a second and sixty.

claude-sessions joins one assistant message by its id, not by its records sitting together (rich-demos-k78j.mk1) (#476)

* claude-sessions joins one assistant message by its id, not by its records sitting together (rich-demos-k78j.mk1)

Claude Code runs a tool while the message that called it is still
streaming, so the call's result, a skill's meta text, or a hidden
goal_status attachment can land between two records of one message.
Joining by adjacency split the message there, and a hidden record split
it only while hidden records were shown. Of the 500 most recent local
transcripts, 14 parsed to a different conversation with H on; none do now.

* claude-sessions joins a message's records across hidden records only, and drops hidden ones after the joins (rich-demos-k78j.mk1)

Joining by id carried a message across drawn records — a call's result, a
skill's meta text — so the conversation was drawn out of the order it was
written: an early call showed the last call's time, meta landed below later
calls, jump-to-parent moved down. A drawn record parts a message again; only
a hidden one is passed over. Hidden records are now read and joined like any
other and dropped after the joins, so H changes what is drawn, never how.
Over 300 local transcripts the structure with H on and off now agrees in all
300; on master 2 disagreed.

* claude-sessions parser's header names the joins ahead of dropping hidden records (rich-demos-k78j.mk1)
